title: Making a music festival management sim for 2+ months
author: thisisnotdavid
selftext:
Tale as old as time (well, 2026): Software Engineer of 15 years, always wanted to get into game dev but life and work got in the way. Started experimenting with Codex + Claude to make the game I always wanted to make and assumed I'd hit a ceiling pretty early. Outside of 3d modelling I never did, so I just kept going.  
2 months and thousands of prompts later this is where I'm at. 70 unique bands, 8 unique stages, 24 different items of clothing, 10 steward jobs, 8 ways for someone to die (I was a bit confused about the direction of the game when I added this).  
I wanted to focus on NPC simulation and emergent stories so I'm happy with the low-poly graphics. The game currently supports 1000 festival goers + staff and bands, each with their own wants, needs and independent decision making. There's socialising, fighting, boozing, pissing, shitting, and more importantly a lot of dancing (& moshing & crowd surfing).  
No real workflow outside of heavy design discussions early on to set the general vibe and direction of the game - I always wanted the process to be incremental and iterative so it's pretty much just one long conversation with Claude, who spins off its own sub-agents for design, build & QA. Coming from a software engineering background I fully expected to be setting up my own SDLC agent workforce to make sure things were built right, but Claude has blown me away in its autonomy. Codex less so, I only use that for the odd image generation now. Game engine is Godot. 3D modelling is through Blender MCP. The songs were generated by Mureka (through Claude MCP), some are genuinely good, others shit.  
I'll be putting it on itch for playtesting at some point. If you want to follow along I'm posting occasional videos to tiktok (Instagram needed proof I wasn't a bot 3 times, so I gave up): [https://www.tiktok.com/@farmtofestivalgame](https://www.tiktok.com/@farmtofestivalgame)

comments.author: Tommyruin
comments.body: As a fan of this art style and looking to implement a similar style in my next project, I'd be keen to learn more about your prompting/workflow for getting the assets (particularly npcs) to look consistent and high quality! Thanks

replies.author: thisisnotdavid
replies.body:
It was basically a lot of iteration: "make this" - review - "tweak this" - review - etc. The models themselves are very basic (I think there's a pretty low ceiling to Claude's 3d modelling without using additional tools) but the pop and cel shading comes from post-processing, which Claude seems really good at which allows you to get creative. I was experimenting with some trippy shaders and came up with this mosaic style, which could be good for a novelty level where you accidentally take some acid.  
Just talk to it about post-processing shaders and you'll be on your way.

https://i.redd.it/3m85zhkzh74i1.png

comments.author: couldgiveaflyingfck
comments.body:
So does the player of the game have the ability to play their own music library? The bands could be real and play their own music from the users MP3 collection. You could even have Claude make an audio filter that gives it the classic music festival sound with slight echo and reverb or, that "live" sound.

If you wanted to go one step further, you could build in that ACE 1.5 music generation LLM, and generate music that could be played at this festival. Look into it. There is a lot you can do.

replies.author: thisisnotdavid
replies.body:
Claude's already built the realtime sound filtering to make a clean track sound live, including varying the quality based on how much you've spent on your soundsystem / engineer.  
The thing with custom music is the live performance is built around lyric timings (singer being at microphone / actions getting livelier at the chorus / fans singing along) and I haven't yet found a cheap, reliable way of extracting that from the music.  
I will look at ACE though, that could be exciting. Thanks for that.
